title: Mechanisms and dynamics of genome plasticity in Candida species
text:
Genome plasticity is frequently observed during the acquisition of drug-resistance in Candida species. The
proposed research is focused on understanding the molecular mechanisms driving genome plasticity in Candida
and the effects that genome plasticity has on the rate and dynamics of adaptation to stress. This molecular and
theoretical research will identify key parameters driving Candida population dynamics and will help us develop
strategies to mitigate the rapid adaptation of these critical fungal pathogens.

title: Specialist in Multi-Scale Molecular Imaging of Tumor Environments
text:
Cancer cells reprogram signaling, metabolism, and other functions in response to changing
environmental conditions. Understanding how malignant cells adapt to environmental stresses
requires the ability to analyze cancer cells in real time in physiologic settings. I develop new
imaging methods to visualize and quantify functions of cancer cells in tumor environments,
providing information and technologies needed to better prevent and treat primary and metastatic
cancer.

title: The effects of sleep and iPRGCs on computations in the early visual system
text:
Mammalian rod, cone, and melanopsin photoreceptors contribute to image-forming visual processes that
encode complex computations in the retina and cortex. Vision also influences behaviors like sleep, which result
in feedback mechanisms that enable sleep as a neuromodulator to the cortical neural code. Understanding how
multiplexed photoreceptor systems and sleep modulate cortical computations driven by complex visual stimuli
could lead to the development of more sophisticated computational models that help improve the design of
cortical prostheses.

title: Bladder cancer PD-L1 control of homologous recombination: Basic mechanisms applied to novel treatments
text:
Bladder cancer is the costliest cancer to treat due to repeated recurrences and low cure rates. We show that
PD-L1 expressed on bladder cancer modulates the DNA damage repair response to afford important basic
mechanistic insights into DNA damage repair and to help show how such data can develop effective bladder
cancer treatments including with novel pharmacologicPD-L1 depletion drugs. These findings are related to
improved treatment strategies in many other important cancers including melanoma and those of breast and
ovary.

title: Sample-to-answer HPV DNA nucleic acid test for cervical cancer screening in Mozambique
text: Cervical cancer is caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV); the availability of HPV vaccines and cervical cancer screening, integrated with treatment of precancerous lesions, provides a path to eliminate cervical cancer. However, this requires multiple visits and access to high-quality, timely gynecology and pathology services, which are often unavailable in resource-constrained settings, including rural areas of the US. To address this gap, we will develop the NATFlow HPV assay, a low-cost, fully integrated, sample-to-answer nucleic acid test that meets the needs for cervical cancer screening in a wide range of US and international settings with limited medical infrastructure.

title: Mechanisms of Juvenile Neurogenesis and Post-Stroke Recovery: Determining the Role of Age-Associated Neuroimmune Interactions
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health given our lack of understanding of the processes underlying
brain repair following stroke, lack of reparative treatments, and high rates of stroke-related disabilities among
survivors. Investigation of the inherent neurogenic capacity for neuronal replacement and the mechanisms that
underlie functional recovery is critical to the development of novel therapies for the treatment of stroke.

title: Single-cell (phospho-)proteomics platform for functional analysis of tumor microenvironment
text:
Tumor microenvironment (TME) is a central component of the tumor landscape. However, there is an unmet
technical challenge for high-resolution, spatial, comprehensive, proteomic characterization of TME. We aim to
develop a transformative single-cell proteomics technology for rapid comprehensive characterization of TME to
meet current biomedical needs. This technology will lead to gain insights into tumor cell neighborhoods, cell to
cell interactions, tumor heterogeneity, and spatial tumor biology for better treatment and patient care.

title: SUMOylation disruption is toxic for SS18-SSX-driven synovial sarcoma
text:
Synovial sarcoma (SS) is an aggressive malignancy driven by the SS18-SSX oncofusion that is refractory to
chemotherapy leading to a high mortality rate. Here, we identify a remarkable therapeutic vulnerability to both
genetic and pharmaceutical disruption of the SUMOylation pathway, including with the in-clinic SUMOylation
inhibitor TAK-981, that is dependent on SS18-SSX. We provide data the mechanistic basis is through
deSUMOylation-mediated re-distribution of BAF complexes leading to DNA damage, cell death, and frank
tumor regressions in mouse models of SS.

title: A Comprehensive Resource for Manipulating and Characterizing the Drosophila Genome
text:
The project will generate genetic reagents that will allow functional studies of 2,000 genes and widen
the the breadth of experiments that can be conducted using new and existing reagents. We also
propose a streamlined in-depth characterization of the expression pattern of all the targeted genes.
These reagents and data often lay the foundation of new hypothesis driven research and support
approaches that use fruitfly in a human genetics centered approach by allowing functional
replacement of fly genes with human orthologs and their disease associated variants.

title: High Throughput Profiling of the In Vivo Tumor Neo-antigen Specific Antibody Reactivity Landscape using PhIP-Seq
text:
In the correct circumstances, human tumors can be detected by the human immune system and cleared from
the body, however, tumors can suppress the normal immune response against them. Immuno-therapies are a
class of cancer treatments that work by increasing our own immune systems ability to detect and clear cancer.
Our immune system “sees” tumors by detecting “neoantigens” or proteins only made by tumors but not by
healthy tissue and we will test a new technology which can better identify neoantigens from tumors.

title: Appalachian Career Training in Oncology (ACTION) Program
text: The renewal of the University of Kentucky Markey Cancer Center’s Appalachian Career Training In ONcology (ACTION) Program will continue a cancer education and training opportunity for students from rural, disease-burdened, low economic, and low education-attainment Appalachian Kentucky. The program will enhance the biomedical workforce by preparing Appalachian Kentucky high school and undergraduate students for biomedical careers. ACTION will also increase individual’s understanding of cancer, thereby addressing the cancer and education discrepancies in Appalachian Kentucky and beyond.

title: Mechanisms of regulatory T cell adaptation to inflammation
text:
Project Narrative/Public health relevance:
Improved understanding of the mechanisms that promote regulatory T cell (Treg) survival and function under
inflammatory conditions is critical to design highly efficient clinical Treg enhancing therapies to treat kidney
transplant rejection and restore immune homeostasis in patients with autoimmune diseases.

title: G protein trafficking in cardiomyocytes and neurons
text:
Many drugs used to treat cardiovascular and neurological diseases act at G protein-coupled receptors
(GPCRs), which can be located either on the cell surface or on intracellular organelles. Cell surface and
intracellular GPCRs are known to produce different effects on cell function, but it is not known how intracellular
GPCRs are supplied downstream transducer molecules (G proteins and effectors) necessary for therapeutic or
adverse responses. This project aims to explain how intracellular GPCRs are able to transduce signals through
G proteins, which may ultimately facilitate the development of drugs with the capacity to fine-tune cell signaling
and better treat diseases.

title: ISU Bridges to Research Careers
text: The proposed program is relevant to public health because it contributes to the development of scientific human resources that will ensure our Nation's capability to prevent disease by graduating students who embark on biomedical careers. The program is relevant to NIAID’s mission because it contributes to a highly trained and health-focused workforce by recruiting and preparing participants from across Idaho. Upon conclusion, the program will have trained dozens of participants who would likely have not completed college.

title: Social experience guides BMA mediated social development
text:
Neuropsychiatric disorder incidence characterized by social dysfunction has increased dramatically during the
COVID-19 pandemic, and vulnerability is especially high in adolescent populations. Atypical social experiences,
like the social deprivation experienced during the pandemic, impact amygdala function and subsequently
interfere with adolescent and adult social. The current project will investigate the contribution of maturing
basomedial amygdala circuitry to social behaviors in adolescents to adults, and how social deprivation shapes
basomedial amygdala function to regulate social behavior.

title: Integrative Dissection of the Genetic Basis for Lipid Subfractions Across Age Groups and Environment
text:
Blood lipids levels are heritable and modifiable risk factors for heart attack, with 1000 genetic loci identified for
various clinically measured lipids levels. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) technologies further enable profiling
lipid subfractions in a large number of individuals across age groups and environment. Analyzing genetic
associations with lipid subfractions will further elucidate the causal roles of lipids for diseases, identify novel
biomarkers to enhance risk prediction, and accelerate the development of novel lipid lowering medications.

title: Investigating the interplay between polymorphic α-syn fibril conformation and cell-dependent pathology
text:
The formation of α-syn aggregation, called amyloid fibrils, is known to cause numerous neurodegenerative
diseases, collectively referred to as synucleinopathies. Given its implication in the disease-specific spreading of
α-syn pathology in synucleinopathies, it is of critical importance to understand how distinct forms of α-syn fibrils
are observed despite their structural diversity. To fill this knowledge gap, this proposal seeks to elucidate the
molecular interactions between polymorphic α-syn fibrils and diverse cellular factors in microengineered brain
tissue, which will provide the structural insights into the development of disease-specific aggregation inhibitors
and antibodies based on the structural specificities.

title: CWRU-Visual Sciences Training Program
text:
Twenty-nine faculty affiliated with the Visual Sciences Research Center (VSRC) at Case Western Reserve Uni-
versity (CWRU) seek renewed support for the Visual Sciences Training Program (VSTP). This T32 Institutional
Training Grant renewal application is organized according to a Visual Sciences Community representing four
major vision science research themes: (a) Retinal Development and Function; (b) Retinal Disorders: Diabetic
Retinopathy (DR) and Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD); (c) Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Immunology of
Eye Diseases; and (d) Genetics, Physiology, and Epidemiology of Eye Diseases. Continued support is re-
quested for four predoctoral positions and one postdoctoral position in all years.

title: Core A: Administrative Core
text:
The Administrative Core (Core A) of the proposal program aims to integrate and manage all projects and cores
by facilitating communication and data exchange. It focuses on four key areas: Administration and Fiscal
Management, Communication Management, Scientific Oversight and Data Sharing, and Biostatistical Support.
The Core’s goal is to support the program’s goal to enhance CAR-T/NKT cells immunotherapy for glioblastoma
treatment.

title: Glucose and glutamine transport: novel targets in cystic fibrosis immune responses
text:
The studies presented here represent a unique opportunity to identify novel targets in the
treatment of CF pulmonary inflammation based upon T cell nutritional requirements during
activation, using samples directly from patients to provide a clear context for results.
